techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.evidence: C2 command 0x07 "Download & Execute"; `dispatch_file_transfer`/Reflective PE Loader (0x23/0x25/0xEC/0xF8) fetches and loads additional DLL/EXE payloads from C2

techniques.name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
techniques.evidence: Manually confirmed in the report's prose, not the original ATT&CK table (and distinct from the pipeline's own, unsupported T1497 evidence -- see excluded_technique_ids' sibling note on T1490 for the pattern of the analyst's table vs. narrative sometimes disagreeing): `get_idle_status()` (Idle Detection, section 6) returns 0xD6/0x2A for idle/active based on >5 minutes of user inactivity, and the C2 uses this to schedule noisy operations -- functionally MITRE's T1497.002 (User Activity Based Checks), just framed by the analyst as opportunistic stealth rather than explicit sandbox detection

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.evidence: `install_vm_service`/`install_minifilter_driver` register `vmservice.sys` and `minifilter_driver.sys` as kernel-driver services via SCM, separate from the `start_vmservice`/`start_minifilter` calls that start them

techniques.evidence: Code Integrity policy to disable DSE

techniques.name: Reflective Code Loading
techniques.evidence: PE loaded from memory without touching disk

excluded_technique_ids.T1490: The report's own summary table row ("Inhibit System Recovery | T1490 | VSS deletion") contradicts every technical section in the same document -- the function tables, the notes' hex dump of vss_shellcode.bin, and the "Sophisticated evasion" summary all describe *injecting shellcode into the VSS service* (vssvc.exe) as a Defender-bypass mechanism, never actual shadow-copy deletion. That's T1055 (already ground-truthed here). No vssadmin/wbadmin/Remove-WmiObject command or equivalent appears anywhere. Removed 2026-08-28 as an apparent mislabeling in the analyst's own table, not a pipeline detection gap -- re-add only if contradicting evidence surfaces.
